chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Ishaq narrated to me, he said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Baghawi narrated to us, he said: Abu Qatan narrated to us, he said: Hisham al-Dastwai narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abu Kathir, from Urwah, from Abdullah ibn Umar, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, said:

Surely, Allah does not withdraw knowledge by snatching it from people; rather, He withdraws knowledge by taking away the scholars. And when no scholar remains, the people take ignorant ones as leaders, so they ask them and they answer without knowledge, thus going astray and leading others astray.

key_terms.فَضَلُّوا وَأَضَلُّوا: they went astray and led others astray

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about how knowledge disappears from the world?
ai.summary: This widely-transmitted prophetic hadith warns that Allah does not erase knowledge from people's hearts directly, but rather removes it by taking the lives of scholars. When learned people are gone, the masses turn to ignorant leaders who issue rulings without knowledge, causing misguidance for themselves and others. This hadith is also narrated in Sunni collections (Bukhari, Muslim), making it a point of cross-sectarian agreement on the importance of preserving scholarship.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 1. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji’abi reported from Abdullah ibn Ishaq, who reported from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Baghvi, who reported from Abu Qatan, who reported from Hisham al-Dastwai, from Yahya ibn Abu Katheer, from Urwah, from Abdullah ibn Umar that the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said:

"Surely, Allah does not withdraw knowledge from the people by erasing it from their minds; rather, He does so by taking away the learned people (from among them). And when there is no learned man around, people adopt the ignorant men as their leaders, and refer their questions to these (ignorant leaders), who answer without any knowledge, thus going astray, and causing others to go astray."
